summary: NTCA urges the FCC to curb wasteful overbuilding in the E‑Rate program by ensuring that special construction funds are only used when no affordable existing High‑Cost‑supported connection is available, and to adopt safeguards that give existing providers the chance to match self‑construction bids. NTCA argues that E‑Rate competitive bidding rules lack safeguards against duplicative fiber deployment and calls for amendments to require consortia to solicit bids from multiple vendors, thereby improving cost‑efficiency and coordination with the High‑Cost program. NTCA argues that E‑Rate should prioritize existing High‑Cost‑supported fiber when it is competitively priced, implement a 30‑day review to ensure cost‑effective use, and prohibit funding of redundant connections. NTCA argues for stronger safeguards in E‑Rate special construction and consortium procurement, including mandatory multi‑vendor bidding, prevention of redundant connections, and better coordination with the High‑Cost program.
